requirements.evidence: Contract is largely present: EntityInvite with HasFactory/casts/entity() (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:10-46), expired() factory state (database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php:35-39), queued mailable with markdown 'emails.entity-invite' (app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:14-50), Entity::invites() (app/Models/Entity.php:41-44), both Livewire components, the manager-only route middleware (routes/web.php:56) and the new lang keys (lang/en/ui.php:78-84, lang/pt_BR.json:864-877). sendInvite/accept/decline/saveRole/confirmRemoval/removeMember match the spec (Members.php:41-209, PendingInvites.php:13-60). Edge-case gap: only expired rows are cleared before insert (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:118-139), so an accepted invite that survives a membership removal still occupies the unique (entity_id,email) index and re-inviting that address is permanently reported as 'An invite is already pending'; onboarding placement (resources/views/livewire/entity/create-entity.blade.php:17) and the tenant session key (PendingInvites.php:47) could not be verified.

conventions.evidence: Good: policies used for authorization (Members.php:37,43,123,131,146), migration has a reversible down() and generator formatting (database/migrations/2026_08_12_233446_create_entity_invites_table.php:11-34), audit channel for writes (Members.php:108-113), RateLimiter used, escaping via {{ }}. Deviations: public input properties lack #[Validate] and are validated only inline (Members.php:25-33,45-48); domain writes (EntityInvite::create, EntityMembership::create) live in components instead of app/Actions/* (Members.php:89-95, PendingInvites.php:37-42); only CHANGELOG.md is updated, docs/database-schema.md and docs/business-rules.md are untouched; #[Fillable] is used while siblings use $fillable (EntityInvite.php:10).

security.evidence: Every state-changing action authorizes server-side and resolves records through entity-scoped relationships: sendInvite (Members.php:43), cancelInvite (123-125), openMember (131-133), saveRole (144-146), removeMember (unchanged, 186+), accept/decline enforce the invitee by e-mail match (PendingInvites.php:19, 56) and inviteRole is constrained to in:admin,employee (Members.php:46-47); output is escaped with {{ }} and no secrets are in public properties. Gaps with limited impact: selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are client-writable state (record id/flag) without #[Locked] (Members.php:29,33); confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval perform no authorization (Members.php:174-182); the custom can:update,entity route middleware is not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware (routes/web.php:56).

tests.evidence: The diff adds no tests/ files at all: change.diff contains only app/, database/, lang/, resources/, routes/ and CHANGELOG edits, so sendInvite, accept/decline, saveRole, removal, the rate limit, the mail and the views have zero coverage, and there are no unauthorized-call or tamper tests.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses RateLimiter, Mail, the audit channel and existing policies, and deletes addMember/assignRole rather than layering on them (Members.php:41-164). But e-mail normalization is implemented twice (EntityInvite.php:28-40), the model adds unused isExpired/isAccepted/isPending/scopePending helpers whose conditions are re-written inline in the components (EntityInvite.php:54-72 vs Members.php:94-99, PendingInvites.php:63-72), and the role-enum ternary is repeated in three views.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names, consistent with sibling files; the two modals and pending list are readable (resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:76-126, pending-invites.blade.php:1-18). Minor drag: sendInvite is ~60 lines mixing lookups, rate limiting, insert, mail and audit (Members.php:41-119), views contain long duplicated inline instanceof ternaries (members.blade.php:87, pending-invites.blade.php:10), and dead model helpers remain.

scope.evidence: The diff is confined to the invite feature: CHANGELOG line, EntityInvite model/factory/migration, Entity::invites(), EntityInviteMail, two Livewire components plus views, lang entries, switcher/onboarding embeds and one route middleware change; no unrelated refactors or new features.

issues.explanation: The change ships no tests whatsoever, although the project requires test-first work and, for each Livewire action, a happy-path, validation-failure, unauthorized-call and tamper test.

Only expired invites are deleted before the insert, so an invite that was accepted and whose membership was later removed still holds the unique (entity_id,email) row and every re-invite of that address lands in the unique-violation branch and reports 'An invite is already pending'.

inviteEmail, inviteRole and memberRole are public input properties without #[Validate]; validation exists only as inline rules in $this->validate([...]), which departs from the project's #[Validate] + validate() pattern.

selectedMembershipId (a record id) and confirmingRemoval (a server flag) are client-writable public state without #[Locked]; scoped queries blunt the impact but the Livewire policy requires locking server-side context.

confirmRemoval() and cancelRemoval() perform no authorization and no record resolution, so a crafted Livewire call from a non-manager flips the flag (impact limited to rendering the confirmation modal).

The new can:update,entity middleware is not registered via Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware, so it does not run on Livewire update requests; the per-action authorize() calls mitigate, but the route gate itself is not persisted.
Creating an EntityInvite and creating the EntityMembership on accept are domain writes performed directly in the components instead of app/Actions/* classes as the conventions require.
Only CHANGELOG.md is updated; the new entity_invites table and the invite/acceptance invariants are not added to the schema and business-rules docs.
E-mail normalization is implemented twice, in a saving hook and in a setEmailAttribute mutator, so one of the two is redundant.
isExpired(), isAccepted(), isPending() and scopePending() are never used because callers repeat the same where-clauses inline, which is speculative dead code.
The long inline 'instanceof UserRole ? ->value : ...' ternary is repeated across views and the role <select> markup appears twice; a small accessor or Blade component would remove the duplication.
The model uses the newer #[Fillable] attribute while sibling models use the $fillable property; the installed Laravel version must support it.
Tenant selection is written as session(['current_entity_id' => ...]); confirm this is the key the tenant middleware actually reads.
The mailable is queued and the audit log written before RateLimiter::hit, so a queue failure leaves a created invite without consuming quota or recording a success audit entry.

review.summary: The change implements invite-only entity membership end to end: EntityInvite model/migration/factory, a queued markdown mail, manager-only Members with invite form, detail modal and removal confirmation, PendingInvites accept/decline, switcher/onboarding embeds, route gate and lang keys. It ships no tests at all (a non-negotiable project rule), keeps Livewire validation out of #[Validate], and has a real edge case where accepted invites permanently block the unique index on re-invite, so it needs changes before merging.
